summary: RE-CHECK of SD-LEO-INFRA-TREND-EYES-OFF-001 at EXEC-TO-PLAN against commits 5f67e932c36 and 8a75a311cec. Verified live, not from the author account. SEC-TE-01 RESOLVED (sweep runs, exit 0). SEC-TE-02 t2 arm RESOLVED (UNKNOWN + named blindness). Step-level secret scoping RESOLVED and complete. Candidate cap RESOLVED, unbypassable, truncation genuinely recorded. NO body text escapes any persisted field or log (runtime-dumped). No-send boundary HOLDS by full transitive import trace. TWO NEW HIGH findings: the SEC-TE-01 fix swapped issue_patterns.pattern_name for pattern_id, which resolves but joins disjoint namespaces (measured overlap 0 over 60 days) so T3 can never fire; and the probe returns FLAT rather than UNKNOWN on a too-short series that live data permanently occupies, with the receipt omitting T3 from both unknown_count and blindness. On FINDING-04: classifier_coverage does NOT worsen the exposure and must NOT be redacted; scope the access instead.
verification_method: Live execution against production Supabase + minted HS256 authenticated JWT for RLS reachability + full transitive import trace. Comments were not treated as evidence.

Three verdicts emitted, 2 candidates, both source tables queried. resolveT2Facts now selects row_data (trend-eyes-sweep.mjs:153-154) and unwraps r.row_data?.payload ?? r.row_data (:161). resolveT3Facts now selects pattern_id/issue_summary (:209-210). No 42703.

Live run confirms verdict=UNKNOWN with detail 'no lesson-channel classes supplied — NOT verified (this is not a flat reading)', and receipt blindness names the reason: 't2: no row carried fix_shipped_at — after-fix recurrence is unanswerable'.

prior_findings_status.claim: Service-role key was job-level, visible to checkout/setup-node/npm ci.
prior_findings_status.verification: solomon-trend-eyes-sweep.yml has NO job-level env block. Secrets appear exactly once, at step level on the single Supabase-talking step (:55-59). checkout (:43), setup-node (:45-48) and npm ci (:50) run with no secret in scope. Top-level permissions is contents:read (:31-32). npm ci uses --ignore-scripts, so a malicious transitive postinstall cannot run in the job at all, let alone in the secret-bearing step. Scoping is correct AND complete.
prior_findings_status.residual: None. `${{ inputs.dry_run && '--dry-run' || '' }}` (:59) is a typed boolean input, not injectable; on the schedule trigger inputs is null and resolves to empty string.

prior_findings_status.claim: No cap on candidate rows per run; unbounded T2 fan-out is a write storm against a 19k-row shared table.
prior_findings_status.verification: MAX_CANDIDATES_PER_CLASS=10 (trend-eyes-sweep.mjs:45). Cap cannot be bypassed: the write loop iterates `items` (:267), which is the ONLY collection derived from all.slice(0, MAX_CANDIDATES_PER_CLASS) (:263). There is no second write path and no branch that reads `all`. Ceiling is 3 triggers x 10 = 30 rows/run. Truncation genuinely recorded: pushed when all.length > items.length (:266), returned as {written, truncated} (:290) and landed in the receipt (:314). The 8a75a311cec refactor from array-property to pair is a real hardening — an array property does not survive spread/map, so the record would have silently vanished on a later refactor.
prior_findings_status.residual: Cosmetic only: a FIRE verdict with null evidence would write one row with evidence:null (:262). No probe currently does this.

new_findings.title: The SEC-TE-01 fix converted a loud crash into a permanently silent false all-clear: T3 joins two disjoint key namespaces, so its numerator is structurally always zero and the probe can never FIRE.
new_findings.introduced_by: 5f67e932c36 (the fix itself) — this is the fresh hole in new review-closing code.
new_findings.detail: The original code joined lane class keys against issue_patterns.pattern_name, which does not exist, so it threw 42703. The fix swapped the column to pattern_id (:209-210, :235) — which resolves, but never matches. The two sides are different namespaces. MEASURED over 60 days on live data: lane keys drawn from payload.lesson_class||payload.signal_type are ['feedback','harness-bug','stuck','spec-conflict']; issue_patterns.pattern_id values are generated identifiers ['PAT-AUTO-b442fd90','PAT-LES-eeeedf0b296b','PAT-LES-1e4dde82cf3e',...]. Set overlap = 0. namedKeys.has(p.pattern_id) can therefore never be true.
new_findings.consequence: reachedPatterns is 0 in every window (confirmed live: both readings show reachedPatterns:0). The ratio is pinned at 0.000 forever. Once the series reaches 3 readings the probe will report FLAT 'disjunction ratio stable (0.000 vs baseline 0.000, delta 0.000)'. T3 is an alarm that is structurally incapable of sounding while reporting a clean look on every run. This is the exact failure class the SD was chartered to detect elsewhere, now shipped inside the SD.
new_findings.corroborating: issue_summary is SELECTed at :210 and never read anywhere — evidence the join key was swapped for one that parses rather than one that matches.
new_findings.proof: 60-day live query: OVERLAP between lane keys and pattern_id = 0

new_findings.title: probeLessonDisjunctionDrift returns FLAT for a series too short to answer, violating the module's own documented invariant, with zero test coverage — and this is the branch live data actually hits.
new_findings.detail: The module contract at lib/solomon/trend-eyes-probes.js:14-17 states: 'Every probe returns UNKNOWN when its facts are absent or unusable, never FLAT. Collapsing the two would let a broken resolver render as no trend detected.' The short-series branch returns VERDICT.FLAT with detail 'series has N reading(s); 3 needed before drift is meaningful' — i.e. it states in its own detail string that the answer is not meaningful, then returns the verdict that means 'looked, found none'.
new_findings.liveness: This is the live state, not a hypothetical. resolveT3Facts.blind === null (declares itself NOT blind) while readings.length === 2 and T3_MIN_READINGS === 3.
new_findings.structural_not_transient: Widening the horizon does not help. days=14 -> 2 readings, days=30 -> 2 readings, days=60 -> 2 readings. The lane-named corpus is structurally sparse, so T3 will sit in this branch indefinitely.
new_findings.receipt_compounds_it: The run-receipt affirmatively presents T3 as a clean look: unknown_count is 1 (trend-eyes-sweep.mjs:305, counts t2 only) and blindness lists only t2 (:352). Nothing anywhere records that T3 could not answer.
new_findings.test_coverage: ZERO. grep of tests/unit/solomon/trend-eyes-probes.test.js for T3_MIN_READINGS / 'needed before drift' / readings.length returns no match. 52 tests pass without ever exercising the branch that runs in production.
new_findings.composition: SEC-TE-03 + SEC-TE-04 + the receipt's unknown_count/blindness omission are three individually-reasonable behaviours that compose into total invisibility for one third of the instrument.

new_findings.title: The no-send boundary is enforced by prose only — the test file cited as its enforcer does not exist.
new_findings.detail: That docblock states the read-only boundary 'is enforced by tests/unit/solomon/chairman-sms-no-send-path.test.js, which is two-sided — it fails if a send import is introduced here — because prose alone does not stop the step.' MEASURED: `find . -name '*no-send*'` returns nothing, and `git ls-tree -r main` returns nothing. The file does not exist in this worktree or on main. tests/unit/solomon contains exactly two files: chairman-sms-exchanges.test.js and trend-eyes-probes.test.js.
new_findings.pre_existing: Inherited from SD-LEO-INFRA-CHAIRMAN-SMS-LANE-001, not introduced here.
new_findings.why_it_matters_now: This SD is the first consumer to build a WRITE path (emitFeedback) on top of that read-only lane, so the boundary carries more load than when the claim was written. The comment actively conceals the gap: a reader checking the boundary finds a citation and stops.
new_findings.current_state: The boundary DOES hold — verified by import trace, not by the comment. See no_send_boundary_trace.

no_send_boundary_trace.method: Full transitive import trace from the entrypoint. Comments ignored.
closed_hops: emit-feedback.js:304 publishVisionEvent(FEEDBACK_CREATED) is the only fan-out. vision-events.js does NOT import any handler module; handlers register only via lib/eva/event-bus/index.js -> registerFeedbackCreatedHandlers(), which the sweep never imports. In the sweep's process getHandlers('feedback.created') is empty and _hookObservers is empty, so publish is a no-op.
Even if registered, lib/eva/event-bus/handlers/feedback-created.js calls detectRecurrence() — a DB read/write, not a send.
resolveFeedbackAudience is a pure string mapper over MACHINE_TELEMETRY_CATEGORIES=['fleet_dormancy']; solomon_trend_candidate is not a member, so it takes the unchanged-insert branch.
no_send_boundary_trace.conclusion: No sendChairmanSMS, twilio, sms_outbound write, escalate_to_chairman, or notify path is reachable from the entrypoint at any depth. grep across all four leaf deps for those tokens returns nothing.

Empirically: anon sees exactly 1 of 19257 feedback rows, and it is the telegram row.

disclosure_assessment.question_posed: Does the added classifier_coverage block make the receipt's authenticated readability worse?

reachability_PROVEN_not_inferred.method: Minted an HS256 JWT with role=authenticated using SUPABASE_JWT_SECRET and issued live SELECTs.
reachability_PROVEN_not_inferred.codebase_health_snapshots: authenticated -> READ OK, rows returned. The policy authenticated_read_snapshots FOR SELECT TO authenticated USING (true) (20260313_codebase_health_tables.sql:51-52) is live and effective. Any authenticated principal reads every snapshot row.
reachability_PROVEN_not_inferred.sms_relay_staging: authenticated -> 0 rows (deny-all, no policy). Raw bodies unreachable.
reachability_PROVEN_not_inferred.feedback: authenticated -> 0 rows (venture-scoped policy excludes trend candidates).
reachability_PROVEN_not_inferred.critical_timing: SVC query confirms ZERO rows exist with dimension='trend_eyes_sweep_receipt'. The sweep has never written a receipt — every run so far was dry-run. This disclosure does not exist yet. It begins at the cron's first live execution (06:00 UTC daily, workflow :23).

disclosure_assessment.answer: NO — classifier_coverage does not materially worsen it, and it is the LESS sensitive half of what is already there.
reasoning: exploration_floor was already cleared and already discloses the sensitive half: the chairman's TOPIC DISTRIBUTION with per-topic counts. Live: [{progress-status:6},{fleet-liveness:2}]. Topic labels are the identifying, interpretable content.

classifier_coverage adds four aggregate integers: total inbound volume (136/week), automated split (41), unclassified (87), classified (8). It adds DENOMINATOR, not content. It tells a reader how big the corpus was, which is exactly what makes the already-disclosed topic counts interpretable rather than more sensitive in kind.

The one genuinely new inference is automated:41 as a proxy for how often the 80-minute liveness watchdog fired, i.e. an operational-distress rate. That is a real but modest incremental leak, and it is an infrastructure-health figure rather than chairman content.

Removing classifier_coverage would be the WRONG fix and would be actively harmful: it is the anti-narrowing instrument added to close SEC-TE-02's sibling defect. Its entire purpose is to make a silently-narrowing classifier visible as a rising unclassified rate. Redacting it reinstates the blindness the fix just closed, in exchange for suppressing four integers while leaving the more sensitive topic labels in place.
disclosure_assessment.the_actual_problem: The content is required by the instrument; the ACCESS is what is wrong. codebase_health_snapshots was designed in March as a code-health table and given a blanket USING(true) read to authenticated. It was never designed to hold chairman-behavioural aggregates. This SD is the first writer to put chairman-derived data into it, which is what makes the blanket policy newly load-bearing.

RECOMMENDATION.do_not: Do NOT redact or remove classifier_coverage. Do NOT redact exploration_floor either — both are the instrument's own anti-blindness mechanisms and this SD exists to prevent silent narrowing.
RECOMMENDATION.do: Scope the ACCESS, not the content. Add a RESTRICTIVE policy on codebase_health_snapshots limiting dimension='trend_eyes_sweep_receipt' rows to service_role, leaving the rest of the table authenticated-readable as today. This preserves the instrument in full and closes the disclosure completely.
RECOMMENDATION.timing_is_the_leverage: Zero receipts exist. This is the one moment where the disclosure can be PREVENTED rather than remediated — after first cron run it becomes a data-removal problem. Either land the policy before merge, or comment out the schedule (keeping workflow_dispatch) until it lands.
RECOMMENDATION.process_caveat: An RLS/policy change is permission-class and chairman-gated per the precedent recorded at 20260802_bound_anon_feedback_ingress.sql (metadata.chairman_gated_ddl=true, 'NOT APPLIED BY ITS AUTHOR'). So this needs chairman ratification and cannot be self-applied by EXEC. If ratification will not land before merge, disarming the schedule is the correct interim.
RECOMMENDATION.severity_if_unaddressed: MEDIUM. Aggregate-only, no content, no identifiers, no dereferenceable pointers. Not an emergency — but it is a one-way door that opens on first cron run.

informational.note: lib/governance/measurement-provenance.js:43 builds a shell string: execSync(`git ${argsString}`). It is reachable from the sweep via emitFeedback -> buildMeasurementProvenance (emit-feedback.js:131) and executes on a GHA runner holding the service-role key. Currently SAFE: every call site passes a compile-time literal, and no sweep-derived or SMS-derived data reaches argsString. Flagged only because the interpolation is a latent injection sink in a path that now runs in a secret-bearing step. Pre-existing, not introduced here.

conditions_for_merge.requirement: Fix or explicitly retire the T3 join. namedKeys (lane signal_type/lesson_class values) and issue_patterns.pattern_id are disjoint namespaces with zero measured overlap, so the numerator can never be non-zero. Either join on a key that actually corresponds, or mark T3 UNKNOWN with a named blindness reason until a correspondence exists. Shipping a probe that structurally cannot fire while reporting FLAT is the failure this SD was chartered against.

probeLessonDisjunctionDrift must return UNKNOWN, not FLAT, when readings.length < T3_MIN_READINGS, and the resolver must surface that as a named blindness reason so unknown_count and blindness in the receipt reflect it. Add the two-sided test that is currently absent — prove it with the same mutation that exposes the current behaviour.

Before the cron's first LIVE run: either land a RESTRICTIVE service_role-only policy for dimension='trend_eyes_sweep_receipt' on codebase_health_snapshots (chairman-gated), or disarm the schedule block in solomon-trend-eyes-sweep.yml:22-23 while keeping workflow_dispatch. Zero receipts exist today; this is the only window in which prevention is cheaper than remediation.

Either create tests/unit/solomon/chairman-sms-no-send-path.test.js as the docblock at lib/solomon/chairman-sms-exchanges.js:22-24 claims exists, or correct the comment. A citation to a nonexistent guard is worse than no citation — it stops the next reader from checking.

verdict_rationale: Three of four prior findings are genuinely and verifiably resolved against live data — the sweep runs (SEC-TE-01), T2 blindness is honest and named (SEC-TE-02 t2 arm), secret scoping is correct and complete (05), and the cap is unbypassable with truncation genuinely recorded (06). The 8a75a311cec pair refactor is a real hardening, not cosmetic. However the SEC-TE-01 fix introduced a new HIGH: swapping pattern_name for pattern_id turned a loud 42703 crash into a silent, permanent false all-clear, because the new key never matches. Combined with the untested FLAT-on-short-series branch and a receipt that omits T3 from both unknown_count and blindness, one third of the instrument is dead on arrival and reports healthy on every run. CONDITIONAL_PASS for the EXEC-TO-PLAN handoff — the work is not in a broken state, no exposure is live yet, and PLAN is the correct adjudicator — but C1, C2 and C3 are merge-blocking. If PLAN cannot hard-gate them, treat this as FAIL.
